concerns.location: plan.md:Phase 1 – Data Acquisition & Feature Engineering – step 1.6
concerns.text: The plan creates a binary “phase‑change‑suitable” label based on latent heat > 150 J/g (step 1.6) but does not explicitly remove the latent‑heat value (or any derived proxy) from the feature set used for model training (step 2.1). If latent heat remains as a predictor, the models are effectively learning a tautological relationship (predicting a label that is directly derived from the same variable), making the validation of predictive power circular.

RandomForestRegressor and GradientBoostingRegressor are trained on the dataset that still contains the latent‑heat column used to define the target label. This creates a circular validation loop where the predictor and outcome are definitionally linked, so any reported R² or subsequent paired‑t test does not reflect genuine discovery of governing factors.
